source: corvint help: the topLevelCommands dispatch list, the root help and each COMMAND --help topic

derivation.commandTrees: each binary with subcommands, the command printing its corvint-command-tree/0 document (every subcommand at every depth with its usage, flags, required inputs and example) and the committed snapshot of it
derivation.exitCodesMentioned: each exit status the help text states after the word exit; incomplete by construction
derivation.flags: every --option token in the command's help text, without the global --root and --help
derivation.freezeContract: the spec codes named in the root help Core header
derivation.globalFlags: every --option the root help Global options block names, including the --json modifier of --version
derivation.globalSchemaIds: every NAME/VERSION schema identifier the root help Global options block names
derivation.maturity: core under the root help Core header, experimental under the Experimental header
derivation.nestedHelpTopics: the two-word corvint help COMMAND SUBCOMMAND topics the help dispatcher accepts
derivation.nestedOperations: the code-declared operation tables one level below an operation, such as docs corpus
derivation.operations: the code-declared subcommand tables plus the lowercase word after the command in each help usage line
derivation.owningSpec: the parenthesized spec code ending the command's root help line
derivation.purpose: the command's label in the root help Commands block
derivation.requiredFlags: per usage form (the command and its catalogued operation words), the --options every Usage block line of that form names outside [ ] and ( ); a form whose lines require none is omitted, and options a help text states as required only in prose are not derived; see requiredFlagsCoverage
derivation.requiredFlagsCoverage: always partial: requiredFlags reads only Usage synopses, and the binary declares no structured required-option table for most forms, so an option that help prose or the parser requires (one of two alternatives, or one required only in some mode) is missing; an absent form or option does not mean none is required, so treat requiredFlags as a lower bound and read corvint help COMMAND before relying on an omission
derivation.schemaIds: every NAME/VERSION schema identifier the command's help text names; input and output are not separated
derivation.selfObservationLedger: best-effort-append when the root help Support boundary lists the command as appending to .corvint/self-observations.jsonl
derivation.workflows: the code-declared multi-command chains in adoption order; each step's usage, inputs, commit, produces, options and example are the sections of the help the step's command prints for --help, its flags, requiredFlags and schemaIds are read from that help as for commands, requires names earlier steps, chain lists the required steps, and a step with a null command is a repository state to write or commit
derivation.writeStatements: sentences of the command's help text that mention writing, mutation or read-only behaviour
derivation.writes: none when the root help Support boundary lists the command as reading without mutating, local-state when it lists the command (in at least one mode) as writing local CEM artifacts or local state, mode-dependent when it lists both

commands.name: cem
writeStatements: prepare Derive the canonical base-to-target patch and write or resume the cem/1.0 candidate at .corvint/change.cem.json.

With --paired-output, --paired-range and --paired-root (all three, additive profile cem-paired-evidence/1, CAX-V0-032) the evidence is read at HEAD of the second repository at --paired-root, both range ends are resolved to full commit IDs (BASE must be an ancestor of HEAD), and the citation is added to the separate document DOC bound to the map's change; the map is never written, so --output is refused.

--replace --expected-hunk-digest DIGEST (given together) first drops the hunk's earlier citations, only while DIGEST is the hunk's current cem-hunk-state/1 digest; a stale digest refuses hunk-digest-mismatch and nothing is written, and every other hunk is kept (CEM-V1-694).
report writes $GIT_DIR/corvint/cem-review.md unless --output names a repository-relative path or an absolute one outside the repository.
report --preview returns the same Markdown in the envelope and writes nothing (mutates false); it takes neither --output nor --format json.
Any language's line coverage works once written in that line format ("mode: set" then "PATH:L.C,L.C STATEMENTS COUNT" per span; PATH is the hunk path or ends in "/" plus it).

--states-output PATH also writes the additive cem-coverage-states/1 document (CAX-V0-010): per hunk, in map order, covered, uncovered or not-instrumented, bound to the written map's SHA-256; the map bytes are unchanged by it.

discriminate Mutate the map's changed Go hunks (at most --max-hunks hunks and --max-mutants mutants each, within --wall-time; defaults 8, 8, 10m) against the _test.go files their test claims cite, and its Ruby hunks against the cited _spec.rb files under RSpec (experimental, TCQ-V0-066; bundle exec rspec beside a Gemfile, else rspec on PATH), and record a discriminates / survived / not-run witness pinned to --target and the test selection digest.

anchor (experimental) Write a pointer to the map committed at HEAD as the refs/notes/corvint note of REV (default HEAD); refuses a dirty or uncommitted map, a map not describing REV's patch, a different note.

With --artifacts DIR, also verify the map against REV as cem verify does and append its verdictSha256 to REV's append-only refs/notes/corvint-verdicts ledger; a different verdict for the same map and REV is refused, an identical one writes nothing.

provenance (experimental, read-only) Report REV's Corvint anchor, Git AI note, Assisted-by/Agent-Logs-Url trailers as untrusted rows; with --notes-tip OID (or --verdicts-tip OID), rollback when OID is not an ancestor of its ref; --verdicts lists REV's verdict ledger records.

export (read-only) Verify the cem/1.0 map as cem verify does (with --artifacts) and require the target to commit it, then copy the map as cem.json and each declared artifact under artifacts/ into the new absolute directory DIR outside every worktree, with a corvint-cem-stable-bundle/1 manifest.
bundle Assemble a cem/1.0 stable bundle for an existing base..target without committing the map or writing the repository.
It writes DIR/stable.json and DIR/artifacts/, checks the map with the stable verifier first, and prints the assembly result with its cem verify-stable next action.
It sets no tier and writes nothing.
The map binds the repository by object IDs; the read is bounded, a symlinked map is refused, and only report writes (its review file, never over the map).

cite, mark, cover and discriminate read an out-of-tree --map under the same rules only with a repository-relative --output, because Core writes a map only under the repository's lock and never in place outside it (CEM-V1-647); every other action takes MAP repository-relative only.

commands.name: affected
writeStatements: The command reads the Git worktree status, builds the multi-language unit graph from source text, and writes one affected-plan/1 document to stdout: the selector's plan (selected units with witnesses and test counts, an exclusion summary, unknowns, scope) and provider.go.packages, the exact import paths an operator may copy into a Go live-test provider bundle.

--format text (AFP-V0-928) writes the same affected-plan/1 plan as lines instead of JSON: "affected <summary.line> worktree=N revision=SHA [base=SHA]", a "warning TEXT" line when the plan read unpinned worktree content, one "selected UNIT tests=N WITNESS <- DIRTY_PATH [via A > B]" line per selection, one "unknown REASON DETAIL [hint TEXT]" line per plan unknown, the exclusion count and digest, and one "check KIND COMMAND" line per advice check with the advisory packages appended.

Example: corvint affected --base FULL_SHA --format text --summary (AFP-V0-872) writes a few-line affected-summary/1 verdict instead of the plan: summary, tiers {counts, summary, tier0, tier1} with the sorted tier-0 and tier-1 unit names a lane runs locally, range {base, paths count}, degradations and warning; --format text writes it as lines ("affected <summary.line> ...", "tiers ...", one "tier0 UNIT" or "tier1 UNIT" per unit).
Example: corvint affected --base FULL_SHA --summary --full writes the affected-plan/0 document instead: every exclusion and every selected unit's test files.
It runs no test, writes no repository state, and never claims that omitted tests are safe to skip; the provider keeps its own NO_AFFECTED_SELECTION_PROOF unknown.

--by-path (experimental, AFP-V0-990; requires --path or --paths-from, not with --full) builds the graph once and writes one affected-by-path/1 document instead of the plan: sharedUnboundedReaders lists once the units the union plan selects as UNBOUNDED_READER (they are selected on any path), and paths gives each named path's scope, how many of that shared set it selects, its unknowns and only the units it adds.

--format text writes "affected by-path scope=S paths=N shared=K revision=SHA", one "shared UNIT tests=N WITNESS" line per shared unit, then per path "path P scope=S shared=J/K additions=M" with its " added UNIT tests=N WITNESS" and " unknown REASON DETAIL" lines.
Write --path=VALUE for a name that begins with -.

An entry is trusted only when it was written by this exact corvint executable for this root, and every directory the graph walked and every file it read or statted has the same size, mode, inode, modification and change time; otherwise, or when the entry is damaged, the graph is built in full and the entry replaced.
The receipt is byte-identical with and without the cache, cold, hit or miss; the worktree status, HEAD and drift checks run on every call, and nothing is written inside the repository.

affected cache (experimental) reports the default cache's location, state (PRESENT, ABSENT, UNAVAILABLE or INCOMPLETE), entry count and bytes as one JSON object, or with --format doctor-plugin as one AFFECTED_CACHE item for a corvint-tasks doctor plugin; it creates and writes nothing.
It refuses a dirty worktree, builds the graph without the cache, writes nothing, and exits 0 when no path is unowned, 1 when some path is, and 2 on an error.

affected jobs (experimental, AFP-V0-2340 to AFP-V0-2346) evaluates the project-owned input declaration of non-test CI jobs (--declaration, default .corvint/ci-job-inputs.json, corvint-ci-job-inputs/0) over the range --base..HEAD and the dirty worktree, and writes one corvint-ci-job-plan/0: per job RUN or SKIP with its reason and witnesses.

In a private shared clone it runs affected on every change and appmap-impact where configured, treats each test whose outcome changed or is new as one that had to run, and writes a corvint-affected-audit/1 report: per change and selector the verdict (SAFE, MISS, UNKNOWN, NOT_RUN), misses, recall, precision, fallback and elapsed time; per selector micro recall and precision and a 95% one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound on the per-change miss rate.

--selection-profile e2e-safe reads one repository-relative application-flow-selection-provider/1 FILE (flows directory, runner config, discovery record, global paths, E2E inventory, per-flow coverage tiers and a coverage file) and writes an e2e-safe-selection/1 advice.test_selection.

commands.name: prove
writeStatements: Usage: corvint [--root PATH] prove --task TEXT [--limit N] [--budget-bytes N] corvint [--root PATH] prove [--limit N] [--mutate] PATH...
This mode is exclusive with --task, --cem, --base and --mutate.
It writes no repository, index, session or ledger state.

The packet modes compile the same document as query (with --task), impact (with paths), or cem verify (with --cem), embeds it unchanged, and writes one falsifiable-packet/0 document to stdout with one verdict per row under proof.rows.
Explicit Go test attack (experimental): corvint [--root PATH] prove --base FULL_COMMIT_ID --mutate --attack-tests
Each Go mutation row adds attack counts and surviving mutant locations bound to the committed blob.
COMPLETED means only that this selected set was judged, never exhaustive mutation or adequate tests.
Only changed lines are mutated, with the same row and invocation deadlines, sandbox and temporary-copy cleanup.
This flag requires --base and --mutate and never runs automatically from a hook.

Named Ruby source (experimental): corvint [--root PATH] prove [--base FULL_COMMIT_ID] --mutate --mutate-source PATH.rb[:START-END[,START-END...]] --mutate-example SPEC_spec.rb:LINE[:LINE...] [--mutate-example ...]
Mutate a named .rb source, changed or not, against the cited RSpec examples (at most 4 spec files, 16 lines each, 16 spans).
Mutants stay inside the given spans, else the whole file under the twelve-mutant cap; the mutation record names the basis (line_basis caller-spans or whole-file) and the selector (target).
--mutate --mutate-runner FILE

Every Ruby mutation run then goes through the corvint-test-runner rspec profile instead of the host sandbox: the baseline and each mutant get a fresh disposable copy of the export under the workspace, removed afterwards, and each receipt carries its own admitted runner_receipt.
test-kills-mutant rows stay NOT_RUN unless --mutate is given (impact and change modes only).

Every mutation row of one invocation shares a thirty-minute budget beside the ten-minute row budget; rows are judged in document order and a row reached after it is spent is NOT_RUN with the detail "invocation mutation budget exhausted before this row".

--mutate exports the packet revision once into a temporary directory and judges every test row on that copy: it runs the cited test file as a baseline, applies up to eight single-operator mutants to the changed file one at a time, and stops at the first kill: PASS when a mutant dies, FAIL when every mutant survives, NOT_RUN with a detail line when nothing was mutable, the ten-minute budget ran out, the baseline failed, or dependencies were unavailable offline.

An RSpec row (a *_spec.rb file claiming a changed .rb source) is judged by bundle exec rspec, or rspec on PATH, against up to twelve relational, arithmetic, integer-constant and condition-negation mutants of the changed lines; every mutant runs, and the row carries a mutation record with each mutant's verdict and RSpec receipt.

Every cited test runs inside a host sandbox (macOS sandbox-exec, Linux bwrap) that denies network access, signals to outside processes, and every write except to a scratch directory emptied before each run and the invocation's build cache; the exported revision is read-only to the tests, and each run's process group is killed afterwards.
The repository is never written.
Without --mutate the command runs no test; it never writes.
The block is read from the ledger, never written by prove, carries no authority, and is absent until a proof has been recorded; corvint observations prints the same rate per falsifier.

commands.name: index
writeStatements: Write the index snapshot of the committed tree for the packet verbs to read.

Writes corvint/index/<object-format>-<tree>-<engine>.gob under the Git common directory, shared by every linked worktree (index-snapshot-v0, experimental): the compiled index of HEAD's tree, keyed by the tree id and by a digest of this binary, so a changed tree or a rebuilt Corvint never reads it.

Eight snapshots per worktree are kept, up to 64 and 1 GiB: the one just written, then this binary's of a tree checked out at a live worktree HEAD, then this binary's others, then another binary's live trees, then the rest, newest first.

This is the only verb that writes there; "context" reads a matching snapshot in place of rebuilding the index and applies the worktree's dirty paths from git status, and falls back to a full build when none matches.
With --if-stale, a matching snapshot writes nothing and reports state "fresh"; a missing or stale snapshot is rebuilt exactly as above.

CORVINT_INDEX_STORE=DIR (operator env var, off by default) makes DIR, a real directory, the store that every command writes and reads instead of the shared one, so a scratch or measurement binary leaves the shared store untouched.

commands.name: flows
writeStatements: Read-only inspection binds declared tracked source and test files to Git and emits application-flow-report/0.
record explicitly writes one screened private evidence file and refuses overwrite; it does not update ranking or accept inferred intent.

Flow variation coverage: corvint [--root PATH] flows coverage --denominator FILE --receipts FILE [--revision SHA] [--offset N --limit N] [--write-back FRESH_DIR | --check DIR] Complete accepted matrices and original /3 receipts; exit1 for gaps,2 for refusal.

export reads application-flow-intent/1 files from DIR (one <flow_id>.json each, plus retired.json) and writes one document to stdout: the application-flow-inventory/1 inventory, the EEP-V1 provider record evaluated at HEAD, or the corvint-behavior-adapter-request/1 built from --envelope, whose application-flows input must anchor the committed inventory bytes.
import writes new proposed intents with inferred links, never overwrites an intent, and prints the written paths.
A listed test whose flow ID collides is reported and skipped, the rest are written, and the command exits 1.
map writes application-flow-map/1: every link with its basis, review state and the self-attested review summary, and per variation the test-run-evidence/0 state and authority at HEAD.
--path or --test-key writes application-flow-lookup/1 instead.
gaps writes application-flow-gaps/1; any gap makes a flow incomplete.
impact writes application-flow-impact/1: flows, variations and test keys reached from base..HEAD changes, with the path of each hop.
stability writes flows-run-stability/0: per aggregate of the flows-run-registry/0 FILE committed at HEAD, the raw repeated-run counts, the applied threshold and a clean or not-stable verdict.
ingest writes test-run-evidence/0 JSONL to stdout.
A bound exceeded exits nonzero with the incomplete code and writes nothing.
None of these writes to the repository.

ingest-coverage writes corvint-coverage-ingest/1 to stdout: the coverage, run-evidence and links inputs pinned by digest; each covered test bound to its one run record, and joined only when that record ran clean at the revision and pins the coverage input's sha256 as a --coverage-artifact; observed tested_by relations from executed source files with executed line spans anchored to the committed blobs; links the coverage contradicts as coverage-contradiction conflicts; and every path or test it cannot classify as an unknown with a reason.

docs renders the page from the committed intents with a fixed template, marks every claim that is not PROVEN, and writes the flow-doc-claims/0 sidecar; both paths are repository-relative and each is replaced through a temporary file and a rename.

--check writes flow-doc-check/0 to stdout and writes nothing: it fails when a committed PROVEN claim is no longer PROVEN or the committed bytes differ from regeneration, unless an unexpired entry of the committed flow-doc-waivers/0 file names the claim, and it fails on an unknown or invalid anchor.

Experimental maintenance (FDM-V0, proposed): corvint [--root PATH] flows docs maintain --flows DIR --page FILE --claims FILE --preview | --apply --expected-proposal SHA256 [--receipt FILE | --adopt] preview writes nothing and prints a digest-bound proposal; apply rederives it, refuses drift, publishes the pair without clobbering and prints a receipt to save and commit.

navigate writes application-navigation-map/0 from the intents' navigation blocks at HEAD: states, and per step its locator, readiness condition, input fixture ID, expected outcomes, effect class and verified state.

Observed application-flow-traffic/0 records (at most 256 files and 8,192 records total; excess is navigation-bound-exceeded) raise a declared read to write-irreversible and never lower a class; an undeclared class is write-irreversible.

--goal writes application-navigation-packet/0: the precondition flows then the goal in run order, each step above --max-effect (read, write-reversible, write-irreversible or external-side-effect; default read) marked requires-grant.
It writes nothing to the repository.

workflows.summary: write an application-map manifest and compile it into an application map at one revision

inputs: One Git repository holding the application's router files and its Playwright tests. The
manifest is hand-written; no command generates it.
commit: appmap.json at the repository root, with at least: schema
a path and a dialect (ui-router-states/0, rails-routes/0 or react-router/0); and tests with
root, specs and page_objects, every directory under tests.root. Add flows, a directory of
application-flow-intent/1 files, to get outcome blocks. A local commit is enough: every later
step reads Git objects at a revision, never the worktree.
produces: Nothing yet; flows appmap build checks that the manifest compiles.

steps.summary: Compile the committed manifest into an application map at one revision (experimental, AMAP-V0).
usage: corvint [--root PATH] flows appmap build --manifest FILE [--revision REV]
inputs: --manifest FILE names the committed application-map-manifest/0 document (AMAP-V0-001,
docs/specs/application-map-v0.md), repository-relative. Build reads the manifest, routers,
flows and tests from Git at --revision, so they must be committed there; uncommitted edits are
commit: The manifest and every router, flow and test directory it names, at --revision.
produces: application-map/0 on stdout. Read it to check the routes, screens, flows and page objects the
manifest declares, and fix the manifest until no unknown is unexpected. Do not commit this
options: --manifest FILE                 tracked manifest path inside the root (required)
--repo ALIAS=ABSOLUTE_ROOT      a second checkout holding the tests (AMAP-V0-017, repeatable)
--manifest-repo ALIAS           the aliased root holding the manifest
--repo-revision ALIAS=REV       read that root at REV instead of its HEAD (AMAP-V0-200, repeatable)
--workspace FILE                read the three root flags from a corvint-workspace/0 file (WSD-V0)
--from MAP                      carry a previous map of the manifest forward when no input
changed since its revision (AMAP-V0-211); re-derive only the
flows for an intent edit (AMAP-V0-240), or the routers, test
joins and flows for an application source edit (AMAP-V0-245);
else build in full and say why (index-admission-changed, ...)
--verify                        with --from, also build in full and refuse unless they agree
example: corvint flows appmap build --manifest appmap.json --revision HEAD > /tmp/appmap-map.json

profiling.authority: diagnostic only; never changes what a command reads, returns, or mutates

not_honoured.reason: internal child workers whose startup verification precedes every goroutine

profiling.scope: every command dispatched by the corvint binary, and every listed MCP server, one profile per process
profiling.written: on process exit, and on SIGINT or SIGTERM
